cohort: 40,964 women with Type-O blood and 40,964 women without Type-O blood who gave birth at a hospital in a multi-center database between January 2015 and June 2018
finding: There was no difference in the prevalence of postpartum hemorrhage between women with Type-O blood and women without Type-O blood overall, but there was a significant difference in blood loss between the two groups in cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Women with Type-O blood had a 1.09-fold increased risk for transfusion compared to women without Type-O blood.
